findings.desc: quality-cleanup: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:549-550 hardcodes the literal string proof-or-stop for the bin key lookup instead of reusing the existing CANONICAL_ROOT_PACKAGE_NAME constant (defined at line 117 and already used at lines 1153/1291 for the same command name). Low risk of drift if the bin/command name is ever renamed in one place but not the other.

packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:558-561,613-616 (inspectGlobalCoreExecutable + checkGlobalCoreRealpath) added in this story a distinct warning branch for a global bin target that is missing/not-a-file (executableFacts.binTargetExists=false), which renders a different remediation string ("...does not exist; rebuild: npm --prefix <realpath> run build") than the non-executable-mode branch. CHK-003:adversarial:0 verificationEvidence (packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs cases 4 and 5) only exercises: case 4 = bin target present but mode 0644 (non-executable, file exists), case 5 = .worktrees/ realpath drift with an executable bin. Neither case, nor any other verificationEvidence for CHK-003, constructs a package whose declared bin target file is absent or is a directory, so the ENOENT/non-file sub-branch and its rebuild remediation string are never executed by any test -- grep for rebuild|does not exist across the test file returns zero hits. This is exactly the kind of drift the story is meant to catch (a broken/missing build artifact behind global proof-or-stop), so the untested branch is in-scope, not incidental.
